name: BUF802IRGTR
title: BUF802: 3.1 GHz, 2.3 nV/√Hz open-loop JFET-input unity-gain buffer with clamps, VQFN-16
summary: An open-loop buffer of gain about 0.97 with a JFET input (50 GΩ || 2.4 pF) and an output that drives 50 Ω, for oscilloscope and data-acquisition front ends, active probes and clock buffers. It reaches 3.1 GHz with 7000 V/µs slew and 2.3 nV/√Hz noise on ±4.5 V to ±6.5 V. On its own (buffer mode) it carries DC to GHz with a 600 mV typical offset; for DC precision a precision op amp closes a composite loop around it through its auxiliary input. A resistor on R_Bias trades quiescent current against distortion, and CLH/CLL set input and output clamp levels.

pins.name: R_Bias

pins.name: VS-
pins.function: Negative supply of the input stage; joined to pin 5 inside.

pins.name: VSO-
pins.function: Negative supply of the output stage. Keep at the VS– potential: back-to-back diodes link it to VS– inside.

pins.name: VSO+
pins.function: Positive supply of the output stage. Keep at the VS+ potential: back-to-back diodes link it to VS+ inside.

pins.name: CLL
pins.function: Sets the negative clamp level of the output. Tie to VS– to turn the clamp off.

pins.name: CLH
pins.function: Sets the positive clamp level of the output, and the upper limit of the input clamp diode. Tie to VS+ to turn the clamp off.

pins.name: Thermal Pad

circuits.title: Main path AC parameter measurement
circuits.description: Bench set-up for the AC figures of the main path. A 50 Ω generator feeds a 50 Ω cable terminated by 50 Ω at the board; RS and a 100 nF coupling capacitor carry the signal to IN, whose DC level comes from an adjustable source through 1 MΩ. CLH and CLL sit on the supply rails, so the clamps are off. R_Bias returns to −6 V through 17.8 kΩ (wide bandwidth mode) or 35.7 kΩ (low quiescent current mode). The output drives RISO into 400 fF plus CL, then a 50 Ω cable into a 50 Ω spectrum analyser input. The composite-loop pins are left open.

circuits.title: Main path DC parameter measurement
circuits.description: Bench set-up for the DC figures of the main path. An adjustable source sets IN; two more adjustable sources set CLH and CLL. R_Bias returns to −6 V through 17.8 kΩ or 35.7 kΩ. The output is loaded by 100 Ω in parallel with 400 fF and read by a high-impedance meter. The composite-loop pins are left open.

circuits.title: Clamp levels set with zener diodes
circuits.description: CLH is held at +2 V by a 2 V zener fed from +6 V through 1 kΩ, with 1 µF across the zener to soak up transient current that the input diode D1 dumps into CLH. CLL is held at −2 V by a second zener fed from −6 V through 1 kΩ. The output then stays inside about ±2 V, and the input is clamped to CLH and VS−. The composite-loop pins are not used.

parts.note: holds CLL at −2 V; anode at CLL

circuits.title: Buffer mode (DC mode) driving a 50 Ω line
circuits.description: A sensor drives IN directly and the buffer drives a 50 Ω series resistor into a 50 Ω load toward an ADC. CLH and CLL are tied to the positive and negative rails, turning the clamps off. Rails are ±6 V or ±5 V. The composite-loop pins float.
notes: V+ is +6 V or +5 V and V− is −6 V or −5 V.

circuits.title: Composite loop built around buffer mode
circuits.description: A composite loop that leaves the auxiliary path unused: the low and high frequency parts of the signal are summed outside the chip at IN. High frequencies pass through C1; the input is divided by 800 kΩ over 200 kΩ into a precision amplifier, whose output reaches IN through R1 (1 MΩ). The amplifier's feedback comes from OUT through Rx, with Ry (adjustable) to ground, and R2, R3 and C2 shape the loop. A switch adds a 50 Ω termination at the input. CLH and CLL are held at ±2 V by zener networks as in the clamp circuit.

parts.note: holds CLL at −2 V; anode at CLL

circuits.title: Oscilloscope front-end amplifier
circuits.description: A 1 GHz oscilloscope input in composite loop mode. The signal enters through 30 Ω and a 330 pF capacitor to IN, which carries the high frequencies; 10 MΩ from IN to In_Bias biases the JFET. The same input is divided by Rα2 and Rα1 (α = 1/5) into an OPA140, whose output reaches In_Aux through 2 kΩ with 100 pF to ground and carries DC and low frequencies. The OPA140's gain is set from OUT by Rβ2 and the trimmer RPOT (β about 1/5), with CF across the amplifier to cancel parasitic poles. Aux_Bias goes to −6 V to turn the auxiliary path on, and 17.8 kΩ sets the output-stage bias. A switch adds 50 Ω in series with 6.8 nH for a matched input; open, the input is high impedance. CLH and CLL sit at ±2 V from zener networks, which limits what reaches the following VGA.

parts.note: adjustable, trimmed so that β is about 1/5
holds CLL at −2 V; anode at CLL

circuits.title: Net input impedance network
circuits.description: The input termination of the front end with the buffer's own input capacitance shown as 2.4 pF. 30 Ω in series ahead of IN and 6.8 nH in series with the 50 Ω termination keep the impedance seen from the 50 Ω source near 50 Ω up to high frequency, where the 2.4 pF alone would pull it down to about 28.5 Ω at 1 GHz.

circuits.title: High-impedance front end for the TIDA-01022 signal chain
circuits.description: The oscilloscope front end placed ahead of a 50 Ω acquisition chain (TIDA-01022: LMH5401, LMH6401, ADC12DJ3200). The buffer drives the chain's IN+ input through 50 Ω. An offset-control DAC adds into the β node through RxΩ. The rest matches the oscilloscope front end.

circuits.title: Evaluation board schematic (layout reference)
circuits.description: The full evaluation board around the oscilloscope front end, with reference designators. Input J1 has a fitted 50 Ω termination R3 in series with 6.8 nH, and 30.9 Ω plus 330 pF (C7) into IN; R8 (10.0 MΩ) biases In_Bias. The α divider is R4 + R9 (13.0 kΩ + 787 kΩ) over R13 (200 kΩ) into an OPA140, which drives In_Aux through R10 (2.00 kΩ) with C12 (100 pF) to ground. Its feedback comes from OUT through R15 (78.7 kΩ) with R21 (10.0 kΩ) and the trimmer R16 to ground, C11 (56 pF) across the amplifier, and an offset input at J3 through R18 and C16. R11 sets the bias at 17.8 kΩ, R12 ties Aux_Bias to VEE, and the output leaves through R7 (50 Ω) to J2. CLH and CLL go to VCC and VEE through 1.00 kΩ; the zener parts for ±2 V clamps are on the board but not fitted. Each supply pin has its own 0.1 µF and 0.22 µF capacitors, with 2.2 µF bulk at the supply terminals. Unused NC pins 13 and 16 are joined to the clamp nets beside them and pin 9 to VEE; the thermal pad goes to ground.

operation.text: Three blocks: a low-noise JFET input stage with its bias circuits, a clamp stage, and a diamond output stage that follows the JFET source and is built to drive 50 Ω and 100 Ω loads. The mode chosen (BF or CL) changes only the input stage. The buffer is open loop with gain just under one; the output sits roughly 0.6 V away from the input (VOS = VOUT – VIN, 600 mV typ).

Only the main path is used: IN drives OUT through the JFET, the output driver and the bipolar output pair, from DC to the full bandwidth. In_Bias, In_Aux and Aux_Bias float. No DC correction is applied, so the offset and gain error of the electrical tables appear at the output. Suited to clock buffers, peak detectors, sensor interfaces, impedance transformation and other signal chains that do not need DC precision, or AC-coupled inputs.

In BF mode the part serves as a single-ended, point-to-point clock buffer for sine-wave clocks; its class AB output, bandwidth and slew rate keep phase noise low, and it can drive capacitive loads and transmission lines.

A precision amplifier and the buffer share the signal. A series capacitor (330 pF) at IN passes the high frequencies through the main path; the low frequencies go through the α divider and the precision amplifier into In_Aux and reach OUT through the auxiliary path. The two recombine inside the part. Below fLF the gain is α/β; above fHF it is the main path gain G, up to the large-signal bandwidth; between them both paths act. Flat response needs α/β = G and fHF well below fLF. Aux_Bias goes to VS– to enable the auxiliary path.

operation.topic: Composite loop without the auxiliary path
operation.text: A composite loop can also be closed in BF mode: the precision amplifier's output and the high-frequency path are summed outside the part through R1 and C1 and applied together at IN.

Diodes D1 and D2 tie IN to CLH and VS–. They carry 100 mA continuous and more in short transients; beyond the CLH or VS– level they conduct and hold the JFET gate. A 1 µF capacitor across the CLH zener absorbs transient current coming through D1. Where 100 mA is not enough, use external clamp diodes and turn the internal protection off with CLH at VS+ and CLL at VS–.

The CLH and CLL voltages set the largest output swing, protecting a following stage such as a 5 V variable-gain amplifier from the 12 V buffer, and the clamp speeds recovery from overdrive. With CLH at VS+ and CLL at VS– the clamp is off and the output swing limit of the electrical tables applies. Distortion rises when a clamp level comes near the signal peak: keep at least 1.5 V between the expected output peak and each clamp level.

A resistor from R_Bias to VS– sets the output stage's operating current: about 34 mA at 17.8 kΩ, 21 mA at 35.7 kΩ. A larger resistor saves current and mainly costs distortion, with bandwidth falling at the highest values. DC parameters do not depend on this setting.
The VS and VSO supply pins are joined inside through back-to-back diodes. The input diodes D1 and D2 are rated for 100 mA continuous; every other ESD diode is rated for 10 mA.
IN steers the output through the main path and In_Aux through the auxiliary path; either can control OUT.

Runs from ±4.5 V to ±6.5 V, split (balanced or not) or single. AC performance is best with input and output centred on mid-supply. The input stage (VS+, VS–) and output stage (VSO+, VSO–) have separate pins to cut crosstalk and keep their transients apart; because diodes join them inside, both sets go to the same potentials, each pin with its own decoupling. Small capacitors (under 0.1 µF) go right at the pins on the same board side as the part; larger ones (over 1 µF) can sit further away.

Keep the input trace short: its inductance resonates with the input capacitance and causes peaking in S21. A small resistor ahead of the DC-blocking capacitor (R5 on the evaluation board) damps that resonance, and the series capacitor (C7) should have low ESL. Use low-inductance (LICC) bypass capacitors (C5, C6, C13, C10) at the supply pins on the part's side of the board, with several vias to a solid ground plane; give the 50 Ω input termination (R3) several ground vias too. The precision amplifier and its parts can move away, for example to the opposite board side. The thermal pad conducts heat but is electrically insulated; connect it to the plane with the most thermal mass.

Because the buffer drives a matched 50 Ω load, putting it ahead of a 50 Ω acquisition chain (TIDA-01022: LMH5401 single-to-differential amplifier at 12 dB, LMH6401 digitally controlled VGA, and a 12-bit gigasample ADC) turns that chain's input into a high-impedance one; the gain, THD and SNR curves compare the chain with and without the buffer.
